map.summary: This area is the local launcher and build/run tooling for a class-recording notes app. Shell scripts on a Mac start the database in Docker, choose a local speech-to-text service, then bring up the backend API, a background worker, and the web page, opening it in the browser. Stop scripts and CI checks keep things repeatable; the whole stack stays on the local machine.
unknowns: Whether the OpenAI client dependency actually contacts an external service is not configured or observed in these excerpts; the stack otherwise appears local-only.
The API and worker image is described as shared, but the exact worker startup wiring beyond a background worker command is not shown here.
Whether failure of optional local speech services blocks app start-up, or how errors surface to the person, is not described in these scripts.

diagrams.title: How the app starts up
diagrams.description: A person runs the Mac launcher, which starts the database, picks a local speech service, and brings up the app so the page opens in a browser.

diagrams.title: How the app is shut down
diagrams.description: A stop script checks recorded process identities, kills the start-up process tree and local speech services, then takes the database down while keeping saved classes.

diagrams.title: How a transcription request is served locally
diagrams.description: A local transcription request is checked for the fixed key, model match, and size, then audio is decoded and run through the speech model on one dedicated thread.

diagrams.title: What the automated checks do
diagrams.description: Continuous integration checks the backend against a test database, applies and verifies database migrations, builds the server image, and separately installs, checks, and builds the web page.

F0001.statement: The API container is built from apps/api, installs ffmpeg and CA certificates, runs as an unprivileged user, and starts the FastAPI app with uvicorn on port 8000; the workflow comment 'Build API and worker image' indicates the same image also serves worker runtime.

F0002.statement: The API package 'meeting-notes-api' declares runtime dependencies for FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic migrations, psycopg Postgres driver, OpenAI client, python-dotenv, python-multipart, and uvicorn, indicating transcription-model access (OpenAI), a relational database, and file upload handling.

F0003.statement: CI runs two jobs: an API job that provisions a Postgres 16 service, lints with ruff, runs pytest, applies and checks Alembic migrations against DATABASE_URL, and builds the Docker image; and a web job that installs, lints, typechecks, and builds the Next.js app in apps/web with Node 22.

F0004.statement: docker-compose.yml provides only a Postgres 17 service on host port 127.0.0.1:5432 with a persistent named volume postgres_data; the API, worker, and web run outside compose (started by dev.sh) while Docker backs the database.

F0005.statement: scripts/cohere_server.py is a loopback-only FastAPI service exposing /health and POST /v1/audio/transcriptions. It requires a fixed bearer 'local-cohere' and an exact model-name match, enforces a 20 MB upload limit, decodes audio via ffmpeg to 16 kHz mono WAV, and returns {"text": ...}; model/VAD are loaded at startup in a single background worker thread.

F0006.statement: Cohere transcription isolates MLX/GPU work on one dedicated thread (ThreadPoolExecutor max_workers=1, thread_name_prefix 'cohere-gpu'), serializes calls with a threading.Lock, and segments audio into runs with max_chunk_s=35 before ASR; failures map to specific HTTP codes (401, 400, 413, 422, 503) and error messages deliberately avoid leaking audio or model exception payloads.

F0007.statement: scripts/cohere_server.py hardcodes local model files under .data/cohere-model/mlx-int8 and uses env vars COHERE_LOCAL_MODEL and COHERE_LOCAL_LANGUAGE; startup must fail if models are missing offline.

F0008.statement: scripts/dev.sh (the 'Class Notes' launcher) requires .env with a KYMA_API_KEY (placeholder rejected), creates a permission-restricted .data directory, uses a PID file with process-identity check to avoid double starts, brings up docker compose with a 120s wait, applies Alembic migrations, conditionally starts Whisper Local (port 7777) or Cohere Local (port 7778) based on STT_PROVIDER, then runs the API (uvicorn 127.0.0.1:8000), the background worker (python -m app.worker.main), and the Next.js web dev server (127.0.0.1:3000).

F0009.statement: scripts/dev.sh registers an EXIT/INT/TERM cleanup trap that kills all its child processes and removes its PID file only if it owns it.

F0010.statement: scripts/export_openapi.py imports app.main:app and writes the FastAPI OpenAPI schema to docs/openapi.json for frontend type generation.

F0011.statement: scripts/generate_fixture.sh produces a mono 64 kbps MP3 test fixture of 1–7200 seconds from a synthesized 440 Hz tone using ffmpeg.

F0012.statement: scripts/start-cohere-local.sh requires a separate .venv-cohere-speech virtualenv, sets HF_HOME to .data/cohere-cache, resolves the model name from app.settings.cohere_local_model by default, forces HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1, and serves cohere_server:app on 127.0.0.1:7778.

F0013.statement: scripts/start-mac.sh is a user-facing launcher: it verifies/starts Docker Desktop, detects an already-running app (probes localhost:3000 and /readyz on :8000), reuses a recorded running dev.sh PID or starts scripts/dev.sh as a child, waits up to 120s for both services, then opens http://localhost:3000 in the browser; it traps EXIT/INT/TERM to kill the dev process it started.

F0014.statement: scripts/start-whisper-local.sh requires a pre-installed .venv-whisper-local/bin/whisper-local and execs it in --serve mode on 127.0.0.1:7777.

F0015.statement: scripts/stop-mac.sh verifies the recorded PID's command line still references scripts/dev.sh (refusing to kill a mismatched process), term-recursively kills the dev process tree, waits, then separately TERM-kills Whisper Local on TCP 7777 and Cohere Local on TCP 7778 only when their command lines match expected binaries, and finally runs docker compose down; saved classes remain in the Docker volume.

F0016.statement: The stack is local-only: PostgreSQL publishes only on 127.0.0.1:5432, the API/worker bind 127.0.0.1, and the Cohere service binds 127.0.0.1:7778 with a fixed loopback bearer token; external network dependency implied by the OpenAI client dependency is not configured or observed in these excerpts.
